Fit an alignment model

Source: R/alignment.R
align.Rd

Estimates the parameters of an alignmentModel() by maximum likelihood, the marginal one with random terms (em()), with the normalization of the values per block of experiments (see alignmentModel()) in the objective; the error parameters and the hyperparameters of normal random terms by default by restricted likelihood. Every experiment, a combination of the columns of the scaling formulas, or with random terms every group, is a separate condition, so the Hessian is sparse over them; trust() and em() take the sparse path as sparse = "auto" decides.

Usage

align(
  model,
  fits = 10L,
  cores = 1L,
  method = c("focei", "quadrature"),
  sd = 0.5,
  iterlim = 1000L,
  init = NULL,
  reml = TRUE
)

Arguments

model

An alignmentmodel.

fits

Number of fits from perturbed starts.

cores

Number of fits run in parallel; every fit runs on one core.

method

With random terms: "focei" or "quadrature", see em().

sd

Standard deviation of the start perturbation on the parameter scale.

iterlim

Iteration limit of the optimizer; with Laplace, spike-and-slab or Dirichlet-process terms the outer iterations of em().

init

Optional named start of some parameters; the intercepts of the biological symbols start where the symbol is the median reading, the other intercepts where their symbol is 1, the other parameters at 0. The coefficients of the first scaling symbol then start where the predictor of that symbol is, per experiment, the median of the predictors at which the prediction meets the relative readings.

reml

TRUE (default): the error parameters, and the hyperparameters of normal random terms, by restricted likelihood, the parameters of the symbols of the prediction (model and absolute of the alignmentModel()) integrated out under a flat prior (Lindstrom and Bates 1990), in at most 20 rounds from the best maximum likelihood fit until the error parameters and hyperparameters move by less than 1e-4. Without random terms or with normal ones and method = "focei"; else maximum likelihood. Where the information of the values and scales is singular, at the maximum likelihood fit or at a round, the restricted likelihood is not defined, and the fit is by maximum likelihood with a warning. FALSE: maximum likelihood.

Value

Object of class alignment: aligned (one row per combination of the columns of the biological formulas: the columns, symbol, estimate and se of the predictor, value and sigma on the scale of the symbol; with REML se from the information of the mean parameters alone, the error parameters held at their estimates), scaled (the readings with prediction, sigma, residual and bloq), parameters (with attribute estimation, "REML" or "ML"), value (-2 log L, of the restricted likelihood with REML, with the normalization and the prior), npar (one less per block), AIC (with REML comparable only between fits with the same parameters of the prediction), values (-2 log L of all fits, sorted), multistart (value, converged and iterations per fit, see plotValues(); with REML the maximum likelihood fits the rounds start from), remlRounds (the rounds of the restricted likelihood, 0 without), seSource ("Hessian", or "Gauss-Newton" where the reported Hessian of a fit with random terms is not positive definite: then the Gauss-Newton Schur complement of the expected information over the random effects), fit, objfn, omega, random and randomEffects with random terms, and the model. scaled also has scaled, the value of the biological symbol at which the prediction meets the reading with the other symbols at the fit (NaN where none does), and scaledSigma, the error model over the slope of the prediction there; aligned has lloq, the smallest such value of the censored readings of a combination.

Details

The objective of an alignment is exact to rounding, so the fits stop at changes of the objective, predicted decreases and gradients below sqrt(.Machine$double.eps), the inner fits of the random effects too.

References

Kemmer, S., Bang, S., Rosenblatt, M., Timmer, J. and Kaschek, D. (2022). BlotIt: Optimal alignment of Western blot and qPCR experiments. PLOS ONE 17(8), e0264295. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0264295

Lindstrom, M. J. and Bates, D. M. (1990). Nonlinear mixed effects models for repeated measures data. Biometrics 46(3), 673-687. doi:10.2307/2532087

See also

alignmentModel(), plotAligned(); the guide chapter Alignment of relative data measurements.

Examples

## Five time points on six gels, each gel with a separate scale and an additive background
set.seed(1)
d <- expand.grid(time = c("0", "10", "30", "60", "120"), gel = paste0("G", 1:6),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
truth <- c(0.02, 1, 4, 2, 0.5)[match(d$time, c("0", "10", "30", "60", "120"))]
d$value <- (rlnorm(6, 7, 0.5)[match(d$gel, unique(d$gel))] * truth + 50) * rlnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.1)

# \donttest{
old <- options(dMod2.outdir = tempdir())
## every symbol positive, on the log scale of the predictor; one value per time point,
## one scale per gel
logs <- c("yi <- exp(yi)", "sj <- exp(sj)", "bj <- exp(bj)", "sigmaR <- exp(sigmaR)")
m <- alignmentModel(d, model = "yi * sj + bj", errmodel = "sigmaR * prediction",
                    biological = yi ~ time, scaling = sj ~ gel, error = bj + sigmaR ~ 1,
                    trafo = logs)
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC -fopenmp]
## a background varying between gels: a list of formulas for one role
m2 <- alignmentModel(d, model = "yi * sj + bj", errmodel = "sigmaR * prediction",
                     biological = yi ~ time, scaling = list(sj ~ gel, bj ~ 1 + (1 | gel)),
                     error = sigmaR ~ 1, trafo = logs)
m
#> alignmentModel: 30 readings, model yi * sj + bj, error sigmaR * prediction
#>   yi         biological    5 parameters, yi = exp(yi)
#>   sj         scaling       6 parameters, sj = exp(sj)
#>   bj         error         1 parameter, bj = exp(bj)
#>   sigmaR     error         1 parameter, sigmaR = exp(sigmaR)
#>   mean of yi normalized in 1 block of experiments
m2
#> alignmentModel: 30 readings, model yi * sj + bj, error sigmaR * prediction
#>   yi         biological    5 parameters, yi = exp(yi)
#>   sj         scaling       6 parameters, sj = exp(sj)
#>   bj         scaling       1 parameter, bj = exp(bj), random over gel
#>   sigmaR     error         1 parameter, sigmaR = exp(sigmaR)
#>   mean of yi normalized in 1 block of experiments
fit <- align(m, fits = 4)
fit
#> alignment: 30 readings, 5 biological values, 12 parameters
#>   restricted likelihood (REML, 2 rounds): -2 log L 389.06, AIC 413.06
#>   maximum likelihood fits, REML from the best: -2 log L 329.79 329.79 329.79 329.79
fit$aligned
#>   time symbol   estimate         se      value       sigma
#> 1    0     yi -3.2127997 0.18302237 0.04024378 0.007365512
#> 2   10     yi  0.4499769 0.05497631 1.56827596 0.086218023
#> 3   30     yi  1.7783403 0.05924187 5.92002292 0.350713229
#> 4   60     yi  1.1659908 0.05670480 3.20910085 0.181971415
#> 5  120     yi -0.1815083 0.05135481 0.83401135 0.042830490
plotAligned(fit)

options(old)
# }
